_comment: Approved security suppressions. Every '# noqa: S<n>' (flake8-bandit) and '# nosec' (bandit) comment in src/ or hub/ MUST be listed here with a justification, or CI fails (util/check_security_gates.py, run by util/lint.py). Adding an entry requires PR review — this is the gate that would have caught the GAIA hub tar-slip (CWE-22), where a '# noqa: S202 - hub artifacts are trusted' silenced an unvalidated tarfile.extractall. Keyed by (path, rule), not line number. See SECURITY.md.

suppressions.justification: git is a fixed, trusted executable; args are a constructed list, never shell-interpreted
'uv pip install' args are a constructed list (no user string), never shell-interpreted
native binary path is an installed hub artifact (operator-controlled); args are constructed, not shell
binds 0.0.0.0 only on explicit caller opt-in (documented flag), never by default
imports subprocess to run CLI setup commands; every argv it builds is literal data from BINARY_POLICIES (see the B603 entry for the same file)

CLI install / sign-in driver. Both call sites (_run and start_device_login) execute an argv assembled only from BINARY_POLICIES literals — policy.binary plus a table-declared install_commands / auth_login_argv / auth_status_argv tuple. No caller string reaches argv: the tools take a binary *name* that must be a key in the table, and a mismatched echo of the command refuses the call instead of running it. shell=False always, stdin closed.

Sandboxed shell tool. Every command (and each pipeline segment) is validated against a whitelist via _validate_command before execution; shell=True is enabled ONLY on Windows so cmd.exe can resolve built-ins (dir/cd/type) and pipes that Git-for-Windows tools rely on. Converting to args-list would break piped/whitelisted commands the tool exists to run.
